title: Datahall evacuation space & power reserve plan
content:
Purpose:
Provide a pragmatic, operational plan for maintaining minimum usable GPU capacity during a datahall evacuation/partial outage and to define a standing power/space reserve policy for on-prem/colocation GPU pools. This doc captures assumptions, simple capacity math, site-level reserve targets, recommended short-term mitigations, and an owner/action list for Q3–Q4 2026 readiness.

Scope:
- Applies to on-prem and colocated GPU pods (H100/A100 pools) that host Dedicated and Private tenants.
- Focus on: rack power, usable U-space for emergency redeploys, temporary surge staging, and safe evacuation thresholds.
- Not covered: procurement timelines for new chassis (separate CAPEX doc).

Key assumptions (validate before sign-off):
- Average rack footprint for H100 pod: 8U chassis per node, 8 nodes/rack (example dense chassis), nominal rack power when fully loaded: 26 kW.
- Typical PDU derating target: 80% continuous load (safety baseline for long ops).
- Baseline pod configuration used for math: 64 x H100-equivalents per rack (logical count, accounting for multi-GPU nodes).
- Normal operating fleet utilization target for inferrable workloads: 60–75% sustainable.
- Emergency evacuation window target: redeploy or absorb 20% of an affected site’s active capacity into other regions or burst pools within 72 hours.

Site-level quick table (example inventory snapshot):
Site | Total racks | Nominal kW/rack | Installed kW | Occupied kW | Reserve kW target (15%) | Estimated GPUs (H100-eq) | Comments
US-West-2-Colo | 48 | 26 | 1248 | 980 | 187 | ~3072 | legacy cold-aisle containment, PDU age mixed
US-East-OnPrem | 36 | 26 | 936 | 792 | 141 | ~2304 | modern chillers, 2N UPS, max rack density allowed 28kW
EU-West-1-Colo | 30 | 26 | 780 | 634 | 117 | ~1920 | constrained floor space for surge choreography
APAC-Staging | 12 | 20 | 240 | 160 | 36 | ~384 | smaller racks (H100 minis), used for pilot and spillover

Notes on the table:
- Installed kW = Total racks * Nominal kW/rack; Occupied kW is measured peak month recent average. Reserve kW target is conservative 15% of Installed kW to cover evacuation staging + temporary redeploy capacity.

Reserve & evacuation policy (proposal):
- Operational reserve target: 12–20% of installed compute power by site (default 15%). Maintained as a combination of:
  - Unpopulated rack slots that can be populated with pre-staged trays within 7 days.
  - Spare PDUs and breaker headroom allocatable by cage.
  - Standby chassis (at APAC & US-East staging locations) that can accept nodes quickly.
- Evacuation absorption target: when a site declares evacuation, other sites must be able to absorb 50% of affected workload within 72 hours and 100% within 14 days via schedule-driven offloads and burst to Hosted API (if acceptable for data residency).

Thermal & power margin checks (worked example for US-West-2):
- Installed kW: 1248 kW. 15% reserve = 187 kW.
- Continuous safe capacity = Installed kW * 0.80 (PDU derate) = 998 kW. Current measured Occupied kW = 980 kW -> headroom = 18 kW (unsafe).
- Actionable conclusion: US-West-2 is under the proposed 15% reserve. Need to free ~170 kW by decommissioning low-priority workloads or shifting to APAC/Hosted.

Surge scenarios (high-level):
- Maintenance window: scheduled PSU firmware roll + chiller swap reduces usable racks by 10–12% for 24–48h. Identify candidate jobs that can be drained ahead.
- Sudden evacuation (power/fire): assume 40% of racks impacted. Prioritize customer SLAs: Dedicated (SLA tier 1) -> scheduled migrations -> best-effort background jobs.
- Degraded cooling (chiller derate): reduce allowed per-rack power from 26 kW to 18–20 kW; compute safe redistribution plan and node-power capping profile to avoid thermal trips.

Operational mitigations (near term: 90 days):
1) Inventory reconciliation: verify PDU breaker labels and per-rack measured kW for top 30 racks (owner: Aaron; due: 2026-02-28).
2) Create two evacuation playbooks (US-West, EU-West) that include step-by-step job drain procedures, IP migration checklist, and manifest of spare kit (owner: Leena; due: 2026-03-15).
3) Reserve pool baseline: designate 6 racks across US-East + APAC as staging with preinstalled PDUs and cable looms (owner: Tomás; due: 2026-04-01).
4) Temporary capacity swaps: negotiate colo SLA addendum for rapid caged power assignment (ops/legal) to accept short-term breakers on emergency. (owner: ops-alliances; due: 2026-05-01).

Longer-term recommendations (6–12 months):
- Standardize rack power billing labeling and install automatic per-rack kW telemetry feeds into Console.
- Introduce a staged procurement for 20 additional cold-swap chassis to cover 2% fleet churn + one-site evacuation reserve.
- Run a cross-region evacuation drill (tabletop + 24h live) to validate 72h absorption target. Record lessons and refine runbooks.

Risk register (summary):
- Risk: Insufficient breaker headroom at colo partner -> Mitigation: SLA addendum + reserve PDUs pre-staged.
- Risk: Cooling failure during peak month -> Mitigation: per-rack power capping profiles + automated alerts tied to Console SLOs.
- Risk: Data residency prevents burst to Hosted -> Mitigation: pre-authorize limited tenant fallback to approved partners or order temporary colocation in neighbor region.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Final reserve percentage (12% vs 15% vs 20%) — tradeoff between cost and resilience.
- Which customers are eligible for forced migration in evacuation events (contract/legal).
- Funding approval for spare chassis procurement vs relying on partner loaners.

Next steps / immediate tasks:
- Aaron: run per-rack kW audit for US-West-2 top affected cages (by 2026-02-28).
- Leena: draft evacuation playbooks and runbook checklist (by 2026-03-15).
- Tomás: identify physical space for 6 standby racks and confirm shipping timelines (by 2026-04-01).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working doc; please annotate where numbers feel off. When we converge on the reserve percentage and drill date we'll convert to a final SOP and attach to the Private Deployments runbook library.

Appendix (quick calcs):
- Example GPU math: 1 rack (H100 dense) ~= 64 H100-equivalents. Installed racks total (US-West) 48 racks -> ~3072 H100-eq. 15% reserve -> ~460 H100-eq.
- If a neighbor region can only accept 120 H100-eq within 72h, then we must spin up Hosted fallback for remaining ~340 H100-eq or prioritize customers.
